quantContext.note: From this project's own scoring pipeline (companies.json + screener.js, Phases 1-5/7), included for reference only - not itself a research source.

whyCheapBearCase.answer: NOC's stock is down 18.0% over six months [source: 1] despite solid ROE (23.38%) and continued revenue growth (see next question), and the 10-Q identifies a specific, quantified cause: the B-21 stealth bomber program. As of Q2 FY2026, the company has 'previously recognized and disclosed cumulative losses of approximately $2.0 billion on the LRIP [low-rate initial production] phase' of the B-21 program, and during Q2 FY2026 alone, cost estimate changes on that program resulted in 'the $329 million decrease in operating income' that drove a 7% year-over-year decline in net earnings for the quarter [source: 2, 3]. The filing explains this was a mixed outcome within the program - 'favorable EAC adjustments on the first four LRIP lots' were offset by 'an increase in the loss contingency accrual on the remainder of the program' [source: 2] - meaning the program's profitability remains genuinely volatile and management continues revising estimates most quarters. This is a real, filing-documented, single-program risk that is large enough to move consolidated quarterly earnings, which plausibly explains investor caution despite otherwise-healthy fundamentals.

revenueEpsTrend.answer: Improving overall, though Q2 alone showed a net-earnings dip due to the B-21 charge described above. Q2 FY2026 sales were $10,876 million versus $10,351 million in Q2 FY2025, up 5.1% [source: 2, 4]. First-half FY2026 sales were $20,757 million versus an implied $19,819 million in H1 FY2025 (derived from the 9-month FY2025 cumulative figure of $30,242 million less the $10,423 million Q3 FY2025 quarter, both from the same XBRL series), up 4.7% [source: 4]. Q2 FY2026 net earnings were $1,094 million versus $1,174 million in Q2 FY2025, down 6.8% - matching the filing's own statement that 'second quarter 2026 net earnings decreased $80 million, or 7 percent, primarily due to the $329 million decrease in operating income...partially offset by a $179 million decrease in income tax expense' [source: 2, 3, 4]. But H1 FY2026 net earnings were $1,969 million versus an implied $1,655 million in H1 FY2025 (using the same derivation method), up 19.0%, and diluted EPS was $13.83 for H1 FY2026 versus an implied $11.45 for H1 FY2025, up 20.8% [source: 4]. The H1 2025 comparison base was itself depressed by a separate, disclosed $477 million pre-tax B-21 loss recognized in Q1 FY2025, so part of the H1 year-over-year improvement reflects an easy comparison, not pure underlying growth. For the full prior fiscal year (10-K): FY2025 sales were $41,954 million versus $41,033 million in FY2024 (+2%), and net earnings were $4,182 million versus $4,174 million (flat), with diluted EPS of $29.08 versus $28.34 (+3%) [source: 5].

marginTrend.answer: Roughly stable to slightly improving at the full-year level, with quarter-to-quarter volatility driven by B-21 program cost-estimate changes. The 10-K shows FY2025 operating margin rate of 10.8% versus 10.6% in FY2024 (+20bps), which itself followed a much lower 6.5% margin in FY2023 when a $1.56 billion B-21 LRIP loss provision was recognized [source: 5]. FY2025 operating income of $4,511 million included a one-time $231 million pre-tax gain on the sale of the company's training services (Immersive Mission Solutions) business, without which the underlying margin improvement would be smaller [source: 5]. Q2 FY2026 operating income was $1,096 million on $10,876 million sales (10.1% margin) versus $1,425 million on $10,351 million sales (13.8% margin) in Q2 FY2025 - a roughly 370 basis point year-over-year decline in the quarter, driven almost entirely by the $329 million B-21 program cost-estimate swing already discussed [source: 4]. This kind of quarter-to-quarter margin volatility tied to specific large-program EAC (estimate-at-completion) revisions is characteristic of Northrop's cost-type/fixed-price government contract mix, and makes single-quarter margin comparisons less informative than the full-year trend.

guidanceChange.answer: Not determinable from the extracted filing text - no explicit forward-looking sales, earnings, or margin guidance range for FY2026 was captured in the MD&A or Risk Factors excerpts pulled for this pass, and none of the cached news headlines for NOC were specific to the company (see sourcingNote). The filing does describe a major, dated, macro-level tailwind that functions as an industry-level forward signal: the Trump Administration's FY2027 budget request, released April 3, 2026, requests $1.45 trillion for defense - 'an increase of 44% ($441 billion) above the FY 2026 enacted levels' - though Congress had not yet acted on it as of the filing date [source: 2].

catalysts.text: Sentinel program backlog growth: during Q2 FY2026, joint activities with the U.S. Air Force on the restructured Sentinel ICBM program 'resulted in a $7.6 billion increase in program backlog,' and the company 'recognized a favorable earnings adjustment related to our recent achievement of certain contract incentives' - a large, concrete, dated positive development on a separate major program from B-21.

One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA), enacted July 4, 2025, allocated approximately $150 billion in mandatory defense funding (air/missile defense, munitions, strategic deterrence, shipbuilding), obligable through FY2029 and expendable through FY2034 - a large, multi-year, already-enacted (not merely proposed) defense-spending tailwind.

FY2026 defense appropriations of approximately $859 billion were enacted February 3, 2026, providing budget certainty for the current fiscal year, on top of the FY2027 budget request seeking a further 44% increase - both filed, dated signals of a favorable near-term demand environment for a pure-play defense contractor.

risks.text: B-21 program cumulative LRIP-phase losses of approximately $2.0 billion, with cost estimates still being revised most quarters (most recently a net unfavorable $329 million swing in Q2 FY2026) - an ongoing, large, quantified program-specific risk that management itself says could 'materially affect' results if assumptions are resolved less favorably than currently estimated.

Sentinel program Nunn-McCurdy breach history and ongoing restructuring: the program was certified for continuation only after a formal cost-overrun review process, and the Production and Deployment phases 'are yet to be priced and negotiated' - meaning material contract-value and profitability uncertainty remains on a second major program.

Bethpage, New York legacy environmental litigation: the company is 'a party to various individual lawsuits and a putative class action...alleging personal injury and property damage related to the legacy Bethpage environmental conditions,' with class certification motions and mediation ongoing as of the 10-Q - a real, filed, unresolved litigation matter, even though management states remediation-related disputes are 'none of which are material individually or in the aggregate.'

verdict.reasoning: The filing evidence supports 'opportunity' more than 'value trap': revenue is growing consistently (+5.1% Q2, +4.7% H1, +2% FY2025), H1 FY2026 net earnings and EPS both grew strongly (+19.0% and +20.8% respectively, even if partly against an easy comparison), and the company benefits from large, already-enacted, multi-year government funding tailwinds (OBBBA, FY2026 appropriations) plus a specific major program (Sentinel) that just added $7.6 billion in backlog [source: 1, 2, 4, 5]. The clearest, filing-confirmed bear case is narrow and identifiable rather than broad-based: B-21 LRIP-phase losses (~$2.0 billion cumulative) that continue to require quarterly re-estimation and directly explain the Q2 FY2026 net earnings decline [source: 2, 3]. Because this risk is well-defined, disclosed with specific dollar figures, and concentrated in one program rather than reflecting company-wide deterioration, and because the company's other major program (Sentinel) and the broader demand environment both look constructive, confidence is medium-high that this is a real opportunity with a well-understood, bounded structural risk rather than a value trap.
